A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EDITLORD and provide readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original material can be matched reliably; v3 principally adds Appendix F.

before.justification: v2 reports original code-editing experiments, component ablations, robustness and length-generalization evaluations, and human rule-augmentation results in Section 3.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds benchmark, generalization, and training-data-efficiency results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Section 2, Algorithm 1, and Appendix D retain the same inductive rule discovery, ADD/MERGE/PRUNE operations, functional specifications, rule-guided training, and inference modes. Appendix F evaluates the existing method.

E1.justification: v3 adds CodeEditorBench's Code Polish evaluation, including Python and Java testing after C++ training, substantially extending benchmark and language coverage beyond v2's evaluations. The seen/unseen CWE breakdown analyzes the retained SVEN-to-CWEval setting rather than establishing another dataset addition.

E2.justification: The original Prompt, CoT, and task-specific Finetuned comparisons remain unchanged, as do the ablation and human-augmentation comparisons. Appendix F uses the existing Finetuned baseline in additional settings without introducing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces CodeEditorBench evaluation using Accuracy, OptScoreTime, and combined time/memory OptScore, plus a decompilation condition using 50% of training data. Existing protocols are retained. The new baseline budget is unclear: Table 9 labels it 50%, whereas F.3 describes full-data training.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, syntactic perturbations, length generalization, and case studies, F.2–F.3 add analyses of unseen vulnerability categories, cross-language transfer, and sensitivity to halving finetuning data. These substantially broaden the questions investigated about generalization and data efficiency.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The original sampling-based security metric estimation is unchanged, and the additional tables continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 6–9 add substantial results while Tables 1–5 and Figure 4 remain unchanged. New Code Polish accuracy is 23.4% for EDITLORD versus 0.9% for Finetuned; unseen-language accuracy is 20.9% versus 0.7%. These are newly evaluated settings, not improvements over v2 scores. Table 9's compilation/correctness labels conflict with corresponding main-table values, limiting interpretation of its results.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, probability factorizations, functional-specification definitions, and rule-set operations are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same methodological contributions and main claims. The headline improvements of 22.7% in editing performance, 58.1% in robustness, and 20.2% in functional correctness are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix F interprets the new findings as evidence of unseen-CWE and cross-language generalization and sample efficiency. A new Impact Statement discusses harmful hallucinated edits in safety-critical software. Section 4's limitations concerning execution feedback and the lack of correctness guarantees remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices A, D, and E retain the same prompts, rule-matching details, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, epoch counts, context lengths, and inference temperature. Hardware disclosures are unchanged, and no new implementation instructions or code/data access information accompanies Appendix F.

R1.justification: Section 5 additionally associates Chen et al.'s self-debugging work with symbolic-reasoning bootstrapping; v2 already cited that work for iterative feedback. This is a limited positioning refinement. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for the same works.

P1.justification: v3 adds an Impact Statement and Appendix F with three subsections, changes author ordering, and updates publication and bibliographic text. The existing scientific narrative and appendix explanations undergo no extensive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: Four new appendix tables display benchmark, subgroup, and training-fraction comparisons, shifting the existing Appendix D/E text downward. Conference information and text reflow produce limited layout changes; the original figures, tables, prompt boxes, and case-study displays retain their designs.

improvement.justification: Appendix F strengthens the empirical assessment of generalization through CodeEditorBench, Python/Java transfer, and separate seen/unseen CWE results. The benefit is limited by problems in the data-efficiency evidence: Table 9 conflicts with F.3 about baseline training data and reverses compilation/correctness values relative to Table 1; F.3 also reverses the readability improvement percentages. These problems weaken that addition, while the original method and evidence remain intact.
